# Data
## First time
```{r import_and_cache_dia, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# ============================================================
# 1. File paths and cache directory
# ============================================================

file_alpha <- "/Users/nvd448/Documents/MSProt2026/Search_outputs/AlphaDIA/precursor.matrix.tsv"

file_diann <- "/Users/nvd448/Documents/MSProt2026/Search_outputs/DIANN/Team2_DIA-NN_identification_results/Team2_DIA-NN_report.pr_matrix.tsv"

file_spectronaut <- "/Users/nvd448/Documents/MSProt2026/Search_outputs/Spectronaut/FilteredCleaned_Spectronaut_Report.RDS"

file_maxdia <- "/Users/nvd448/Documents/MSProt2026/Search_outputs/MaxQuant/Team4_MaxDIA_evidence.txt"

cache_dir <- "/Users/nvd448/Documents/MSProt2026/R_cache"

dir.create(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# ============================================================
# 2. AlphaDIA — preserve precursor hashes as character
# ============================================================

alpha_cache <- file.path(cache_dir, "alpha_raw_character_hash.rds")

if (file.exists(alpha_cache)) {

  alpha_raw <- readRDS(alpha_cache)

} else {

  alpha_raw <- readr::read_tsv(
    file_alpha,
    col_types = readr::cols(
      precursor.mod_seq_charge_hash = readr::col_character(),
      .default = readr::col_guess()
    ),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

  saveRDS(alpha_raw, alpha_cache, compress = FALSE)
}

# ============================================================
# 3. DIA-NN — original wide matrix
# ============================================================

diann_cache <- file.path(cache_dir, "diann_raw.rds")

if (file.exists(diann_cache)) {

  diann_raw <- readRDS(diann_cache)

} else {

  diann_raw <- readr::read_tsv(
    file_diann,
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

  saveRDS(diann_raw, diann_cache, compress = FALSE)
}

# ============================================================
# 4. Spectronaut — already saved as RDS
# ============================================================

spectronaut_raw <- readRDS(file_spectronaut)

# ============================================================
# 5. MaxDIA — import essential columns with explicit types
# ============================================================

maxdia_cache <- file.path(cache_dir, "maxdia_selected_typed.rds")

if (file.exists(maxdia_cache)) {

  maxdia_raw <- readRDS(maxdia_cache)

} else {

  maxdia_header <- names(
    readr::read_tsv(
      file_maxdia,
      n_max = 0,
      show_col_types = FALSE
    )
  )

  keep_cols <- c(
    "Raw file",
    "Modified sequence",
    "Sequence",
    "Charge",
    "Leading proteins",
    "Proteins",
    "Intensity",
    "Q-value",
    "PEP",
    "Reverse",
    "Potential contaminant",
    "DIA evidence type"
  )

  missing_cols <- setdiff(keep_cols, maxdia_header)

  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop(
      "Missing MaxDIA columns: ",
      paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }

  column_spec <- readr::cols(
    .default = readr::col_skip(),

    `Raw file` = readr::col_character(),
    `Modified sequence` = readr::col_character(),
    Sequence = readr::col_character(),
    Charge = readr::col_integer(),
    `Leading proteins` = readr::col_character(),
    Proteins = readr::col_character(),
    Intensity = readr::col_double(),
    `Q-value` = readr::col_double(),
    PEP = readr::col_double(),
    Reverse = readr::col_character(),
    `Potential contaminant` = readr::col_character(),
    `DIA evidence type` = readr::col_character()
  )

  maxdia_raw <- readr::read_tsv(
    file_maxdia,
    col_types = column_spec,
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

  saveRDS(maxdia_raw, maxdia_cache, compress = FALSE)
}

# ============================================================
# 6. Verify imported datasets
# ============================================================

import_summary <- tibble(
  Software = c("AlphaDIA", "DIANN", "Spectronaut", "MaxDIA"),
  Rows = c(
    nrow(alpha_raw),
    nrow(diann_raw),
    nrow(spectronaut_raw),
    nrow(maxdia_raw)
  ),
  Columns = c(
    ncol(alpha_raw),
    ncol(diann_raw),
    ncol(spectronaut_raw),
    ncol(maxdia_raw)
  )
)

print(import_summary)

# Verify identifier types
class(alpha_raw$precursor.mod_seq_charge_hash)
class(diann_raw$Precursor.Id)
class(spectronaut_raw$EG.PrecursorId)
class(maxdia_raw$`Modified sequence`)
```

## Hemogenize datasets
```{r homogenize_datasets, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# ============================================================
# 1. AlphaDIA: wide -> long
# ============================================================

alpha_run_cols <- names(alpha_raw)[2:85]

alpha_long <- alpha_raw |>
  rename(
    Precursor.Id = precursor.mod_seq_charge_hash,
    Stripped.Sequence = precursor.sequence,
    Precursor.Charge = precursor.charge,
    Protein.Group = pg.name
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(alpha_run_cols),
    names_to = "Run",
    values_to = "Precursor.Quantity"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Precursor.Id = as.character(Precursor.Id),
    Run = str_remove(
      basename(Run),
      regex("\\.raw$", ignore_case = TRUE)
    )
  )

# ============================================================
# 2. DIA-NN: wide -> long
# ============================================================

diann_run_cols <- names(diann_raw)[11:94]

diann_long <- diann_raw |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(diann_run_cols),
    names_to = "Run",
    values_to = "Precursor.Quantity"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Precursor.Id = as.character(Precursor.Id),
    Run = str_remove(
      basename(Run),
      regex("\\.raw$", ignore_case = TRUE)
    )
  )

# ============================================================
# 3. Spectronaut: long -> standardized long
# ============================================================

spectronaut_long <- spectronaut_raw |>
  rename(
    Run = R.FileName,
    Precursor.Id = EG.PrecursorId,
    Stripped.Sequence = PEP.StrippedSequence,
    Protein.Group = PG.ProteinGroups,
    Precursor.Quantity = FG.Quantity,
    PEP = EG.PEP,
    Cscore = EG.Cscore,
    Decoy = EG.IsDecoy,
    IsImputed = EG.IsImputed
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Run = str_remove(
      basename(Run),
      regex("\\.raw$", ignore_case = TRUE)
    ),
    Precursor.Id = as.character(Precursor.Id)
  )

# ============================================================
# 4. MaxDIA: long -> standardized long
# ============================================================

maxdia_long <- maxdia_raw |>
  rename(
    Run = `Raw file`,
    Modified.Sequence = `Modified sequence`,
    Stripped.Sequence = Sequence,
    Precursor.Charge = Charge,
    Protein.Group = `Leading proteins`,
    Protein.Ids = Proteins,
    Precursor.Quantity = Intensity,
    Q.Value = `Q-value`,
    DIA.evidence.type = `DIA evidence type`
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Run = str_remove(
      basename(Run),
      regex("\\.raw$", ignore_case = TRUE)
    ),
    Precursor.Id = paste(
      Modified.Sequence,
      Precursor.Charge,
      sep = "_"
    )
  )

# ============================================================
# 5. Store standardized datasets in a list
# ============================================================

dia_long <- list(
  AlphaDIA = alpha_long,
  DIANN = diann_long,
  Spectronaut = spectronaut_long,
  MaxDIA = maxdia_long
)

# ============================================================
# 6. Check dimensions and number of runs
# ============================================================

format_summary <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  dia_long,
  function(dat, software) {
    tibble(
      Software = software,
      Rows = nrow(dat),
      Columns = ncol(dat),
      Runs = n_distinct(dat$Run)
    )
  }
)

print(format_summary)

```

Each row in the precursor data table is in “long format” and contains information about one precursor in a specific run.

The sample annotation table is not available and can be generated from the run labels, as the researchers included information on the design in the filenames.

```{r sample_annotation}
# ============================================================
# Generate sample annotations from run filenames
# ============================================================

make_annotation <- function(data) {

  tibble(
    runCol = unique(data$Run)
  ) |>
    mutate(
      # Standardize run names
      sampleId = basename(runCol),
      sampleId = str_remove(
        sampleId,
        regex("\\.(raw|mzML)$", ignore_case = TRUE)
      ),

      # Sample-set prefix (meaning to be confirmed)
      sample_set = str_extract(sampleId, "^Group[1-4]"),

      # Genotype
      genotype = case_when(
        str_detect(sampleId, regex("c-jun_KO", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "KO",
        str_detect(sampleId, regex("CTRL", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "CTRL",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),

      # Drug treatment
      treatment = case_when(
        str_detect(sampleId, regex("JNK-IN-8", ignore_case = TRUE)) &
          str_detect(sampleId, regex("cDDP", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "JNK_IN_8_cDDP",

        str_detect(sampleId, regex("JNK-IN-8", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "JNK_IN_8",

        str_detect(sampleId, regex("cDDP", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "cDDP",

        TRUE ~ "Untreated"
      ),

      # Treatment duration
      time = case_when(
        str_detect(sampleId, regex("06h", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "6h",
        str_detect(sampleId, regex("24h", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "24h",
        treatment == "Untreated" ~ "Baseline",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),

      # Final numeric suffix in the filename
      rep = str_extract(sampleId, "[0-9]+$"),

      # Combined experimental condition
      condition = case_when(
        !is.na(genotype) & !is.na(time) ~
          paste(genotype, treatment, time, sep = "_"),
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),

      genotype = factor(genotype),
      treatment = factor(treatment),
      time = factor(time),
      condition = factor(condition),
      rep = factor(rep)
    ) |>
    arrange(sampleId)
}

# ============================================================
# Apply the function to all four datasets
# ============================================================

annot <- purrr::map(
  precursors,
  make_annotation
)

# ============================================================
# Inspect sample annotations
# ============================================================

# Number of runs per software
purrr::map_int(annot, nrow)

# Number of samples per experimental condition
purrr::map(
  annot,
  ~ count(.x, condition, name = "n_samples")
)

# Check whether any filenames could not be classified
purrr::map(
  annot,
  ~ filter(.x, is.na(genotype) | is.na(time))
)

# Verify that all software packages have identical sample IDs
identical_sample_ids <- all(
  purrr::map_lgl(
    annot,
    ~ identical(.x$sampleId, annot$DIANN$sampleId)
  )
)

cat("Identical sample IDs and order:", identical_sample_ids, "\n")

# Check missing annotation fields
purrr::imap_dfr(
  annot,
  ~ tibble(
    Software = .y,
    Missing_Genotype = sum(is.na(.x$genotype)),
    Missing_Treatment = sum(is.na(.x$treatment)),
    Missing_Time = sum(is.na(.x$time)),
    Missing_Condition = sum(is.na(.x$condition)),
    Duplicate_Sample_IDs = sum(duplicated(.x$sampleId))
  )
)
```
## Qfeatures
Here, Precursor.Quantity provides the quantitative values, and Precursor.Id identifies the precursor features.
```{r resolve_duplicate_precursors, message=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Resolve duplicate precursor-run records before QFeatures
# Only Spectronaut and MaxDIA
# ============================================================

# AlphaDIA and DIA-NN already have unique precursor-run keys
alpha_qf_input <- alpha_precursors
diann_qf_input <- diann_precursors

# Spectronaut:
# Prefer nonmissing quantity, lowest PEP, highest Cscore
spectronaut_qf_input <- spectronaut_precursors |>
  arrange(
    Run,
    Precursor.Id,
    is.na(Precursor.Quantity),
    PEP,
    desc(Cscore)
  ) |>
  distinct(Run, Precursor.Id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# MaxDIA:
# Prefer nonmissing quantity, lowest PEP, lowest Q.Value
maxdia_qf_input <- maxdia_precursors |>
  arrange(
    Run,
    Precursor.Id,
    is.na(Precursor.Quantity),
    PEP,
    Q.Value
  ) |>
  distinct(Run, Precursor.Id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Store QFeatures input tables
precursors_qf <- list(
  AlphaDIA = alpha_qf_input,
  DIANN = diann_qf_input,
  Spectronaut = spectronaut_qf_input,
  MaxDIA = maxdia_qf_input
)

# Validate unique precursor-run identifiers
duplicate_validation <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  precursors_qf,
  function(dat, software) {
    tibble(
      Software = software,
      Rows = nrow(dat),
      Runs = n_distinct(dat$Run),
      Duplicate_Keys = nrow(dat) -
        data.table::uniqueN(
          data.table::as.data.table(
            dat[, c("Run", "Precursor.Id")]
          ),
          by = c("Run", "Precursor.Id")
        ),
      Zero_Quantities = sum(dat$Precursor.Quantity == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      Missing_Quantities = sum(is.na(dat$Precursor.Quantity))
    )
  }
)

print(duplicate_validation, width = Inf)
```

```{r create_qfeatures, message=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Create and cache deduplicated QFeatures objects
# One QFeatures object per software
# No identification-confidence or intensity filtering
# ============================================================

cache_dir <- "/Users/nvd448/Documents/MSProt2026/R_cache"

dir.create(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

software_names <- c("AlphaDIA", "DIANN", "Spectronaut", "MaxDIA")

# Cache paths for deduplicated, otherwise unfiltered data
qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(
    cache_dir,
    paste0("qf_", software_names, "_deduplicated.rds")
  ),
  software_names
)

# Verify duplicate resolution before QFeatures creation
if (any(duplicate_validation$Duplicate_Keys != 0)) {
  stop("Duplicate precursor-run identifiers remain.")
}

# Create and cache one software at a time
for (software in software_names) {

  qf_file <- qf_files[[software]]

  if (file.exists(qf_file)) {
    message(software, ": deduplicated cache already exists. Skipping.")
    next
  }

  message("Creating QFeatures for ", software, "...")

  # Use original precursor data after duplicate resolution
  dat <- precursors_qf[[software]]

  qf_one <- readQFeatures(
    assayData = dat,
    colData = annot[[software]],
    quantCols = "Precursor.Quantity",
    runCol = "Run",
    fnames = "Precursor.Id"
  )

  # Save to temporary file first
  temp_file <- paste0(qf_file, ".tmp")

  saveRDS(qf_one, temp_file)

  if (!file.rename(temp_file, qf_file)) {
    stop("Could not finalize QFeatures cache for ", software)
  }

  message(software, ": saved to ", qf_file)

  # Release memory before processing next software
  rm(dat, qf_one)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

message("Deduplicated QFeatures cache creation finished.")
```

```{r inspect_qfeatures_all, message=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Initial inspection of unfiltered precursor-level QFeatures
# ============================================================

qf_summary <- list()
run_summary <- list()

for (software in software_names) {

  message("Inspecting ", software, "...")

  # Load only one QFeatures object
  qf_one <- readRDS(qf_files[[software]])

  # Each assay represents one LC-MS run
  run_names <- names(qf_one)

  n_precursors <- vapply(
    seq_along(qf_one),
    function(i) nrow(qf_one[[i]]),
    integer(1)
  )

  # Overall summary
  qf_summary[[software]] <- tibble(
    Software = software,
    Assays = length(qf_one),
    Total_Observations = sum(n_precursors),
    Min_Precursors_Per_Run = min(n_precursors),
    Median_Precursors_Per_Run = median(n_precursors),
    Max_Precursors_Per_Run = max(n_precursors)
  )

  # Per-run precursor counts
  run_summary[[software]] <- tibble(
    Software = software,
    Run = run_names,
    N_Precursors = n_precursors
  )

  rm(qf_one)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

qf_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(qf_summary)
run_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(run_summary)

print(qf_summary, width = Inf)
```

# Data preprocessing
The data preprocessing workflow for DIA data is similar to the workflow for DDA-LFQ data, but there are suble differences as we start from precursor level data and have additional columns. 

## Missing values
The first preprocessing step is to correctly encode the missing values. It is important that missing values are encoded using `NA`. For instance, non-observed values should not be encoded with a zero because true zeros (the proteomic feature is absent from the sample) cannot be distinguished from technical zeros (the feature was missed by the instrument or could not be identified). We therefore replace any zero in the quantitative data with an `NA`.

```{r count_zero_intensities, message=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Count zero and missing precursor intensities before zeroIsNA
# ============================================================

software_names <- c("AlphaDIA", "DIANN", "Spectronaut", "MaxDIA")

zero_summary <- vector("list", length(software_names))
names(zero_summary) <- software_names

zero_by_run <- vector("list", length(software_names))
names(zero_by_run) <- software_names

for (software in software_names) {

  message("Checking zero intensities: ", software)

  # Load one cached QFeatures object at a time
  qf_one <- readRDS(qf_files[[software]])

  # Count values in each run-specific assay
  run_counts <- purrr::map_dfr(
    seq_along(qf_one),
    function(i) {

      x <- assay(qf_one[[i]])

      tibble(
        Software = software,
        Run = names(qf_one)[i],
        Total_Values = length(x),
        Zero_Values = sum(x == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
        Missing_Values = sum(is.na(x)),
        Nonpositive_Values = sum(x < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
      )
    }
  )

  zero_by_run[[software]] <- run_counts

  zero_summary[[software]] <- run_counts |>
    summarise(
      Software = first(Software),
      Runs = n(),
      Total_Values = sum(Total_Values),
      Zero_Values = sum(Zero_Values),
      Missing_Values = sum(Missing_Values),
      Nonpositive_Values = sum(Nonpositive_Values)
    )

  rm(qf_one, run_counts)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

zero_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(zero_summary)
zero_by_run <- dplyr::bind_rows(zero_by_run)

print(zero_summary, width = Inf)
```

Inspection of the precursor-level QFeatures objects revealed differences in how missing measurements are represented across the four DIA software packages. AlphaDIA contained 324,817 precursor entries in each of the 84 runs, with 13,010,298 intensity values encoded as zeros. DIA-NN and Spectronaut already represented missing intensity measurements as NA, with 10,497,983 and 49 missing values, respectively, in the QFeatures objects. In contrast, MaxDIA contained 15,350,731 precursor observations across 84 runs, with varying numbers of precursor entries per run and no explicit zeros or NA values. These differences indicate that AlphaDIA represents unquantified precursor measurements as zeros, DIA-NN and Spectronaut use explicit NA values for missing measurements, and MaxDIA reports only available precursor records. However, the absence of explicit missing values does not imply complete precursor coverage across runs, as unreported precursor–run combinations may be absent from the individual assays. Therefore, AlphaDIA's zero intensities will be converted to NA using zeroIsNA(), while missing precursor–run combinations will be accounted for when aligning precursor identifiers across runs.

```{r}
# Convert zero intensities to NA in all 84 assays
qf_alpha <- zeroIsNA(qf_alpha, names(qf_alpha))
```

## Joining assay
Combine 84 run-specific assays into one precursor assay for each DIA software:

```{r combine_qfeatures_all, message=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Combine 84 assays into one precursor-level assay per software
# Validate assay, rowData and colData
# Save each software separately
# ============================================================

software_names <- c("AlphaDIA", "DIANN", "Spectronaut", "MaxDIA")

combined_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(
    cache_dir,
    paste0("qf_", software_names, "_combined.rds")
  ),
  software_names
)

for (software in software_names) {

  message("Processing ", software, "...")

  output_file <- combined_qf_files[[software]]

  if (file.exists(output_file)) {
    message("Combined cache already exists: ", software)
    next
  }

  # Load one software at a time
  qf_one <- readRDS(qf_files[[software]])

  # Convert AlphaDIA zero intensities to NA
  if (software == "AlphaDIA") {
    qf_one <- zeroIsNA(qf_one, names(qf_one))
  }

  # Join all 84 run-specific assays by precursor identifier
  qf_combined <- joinAssays(
    qf_one,
    i = names(qf_one),
    name = "precursors"
  )

  # Keep only the combined assay
  qf_combined <- qf_combined[, , "precursors"]

  # Extract sample annotations from QFeatures
  sample_metadata <- as.data.frame(colData(qf_combined))

  # Match annotations to assay columns
  run_names <- colnames(qf_combined[["precursors"]])

  stopifnot(
    length(run_names) == 84L,
    !anyDuplicated(run_names),
    all(run_names %in% rownames(sample_metadata))
  )

  sample_metadata <- sample_metadata[
    run_names,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  # Attach sample annotations directly to combined assay
  colData(qf_combined[["precursors"]]) <-
    S4Vectors::DataFrame(sample_metadata)

  # Validate dimensions and annotation alignment
  se <- qf_combined[["precursors"]]

  stopifnot(
    ncol(se) == 84L,
    nrow(rowData(se)) == nrow(se),
    nrow(colData(se)) == ncol(se),
    identical(rownames(colData(se)), colnames(se))
  )

  # Check remaining zeros and missing values
  x <- assay(se)

  n_zeros <- sum(x == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  n_missing <- sum(is.na(x))

  if (software == "AlphaDIA" && n_zeros != 0) {
    stop("AlphaDIA still contains zero intensities.")
  }

  message(
    software,
    ": ", nrow(se), " precursors × ", ncol(se), " runs",
    "; zeros = ", n_zeros,
    "; NA = ", n_missing
  )

  # Save using a temporary file
  temp_file <- paste0(output_file, ".tmp")

  saveRDS(qf_combined, temp_file)

  if (!file.rename(temp_file, output_file)) {
    stop("Could not save combined QFeatures for ", software)
  }

  message("Saved: ", output_file)

  # Release memory
  rm(qf_one, qf_combined, se, x, sample_metadata)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

message("All four combined QFeatures objects are ready.")
```

## Filtering
```{r filter_combined_precursors, message=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Filter combined precursor-level QFeatures
#
# 1. Detection in >= 2/3 of samples in ANY condition
# 2. Remove decoys, reverse hits and contaminants
# 3. Retain proteotypic peptides where identifiable
# 4. Do NOT remove proteins supported by only one peptide
#
# IMPORTANT:
# Proteotypic status cannot yet be verified for AlphaDIA
# and Spectronaut using their current combined rowData.
# ============================================================

software_names <- c(
  "AlphaDIA", "DIANN", "Spectronaut", "MaxDIA"
)

filtered_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(
    cache_dir,
    paste0("qf_", software_names, "_filtered_final.rds")
  ),
  software_names
)

filter_summary <- list()

# Helper: nonmissing, nonempty text
valid_text <- function(z) {
  !is.na(z) & nzchar(trimws(as.character(z)))
}

# Helper: annotations indicating an unflagged entry
# Supports logical FALSE, numeric 0, and MaxQuant-style "-"
not_flagged <- function(z) {
  z <- tolower(trimws(as.character(z)))

  is.na(z) | z %in% c("", "-", "0", "false")
}

for (software in software_names) {

  message("Filtering ", software, "...")

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. Load one combined QFeatures object
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  qf_one <- readRDS(combined_qf_files[[software]])
  se <- qf_one[["precursors"]]

  rd <- as.data.frame(rowData(se))
  cd <- as.data.frame(colData(se))

  n_before <- nrow(se)

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. Condition-aware detection filter
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  conditions <- as.character(cd$condition)

  stopifnot(
    length(conditions) == ncol(se),
    !anyNA(conditions),
    identical(rownames(cd), colnames(se))
  )

  groups <- split(seq_along(conditions), conditions)

  keep_detection <- rep(FALSE, n_before)

  for (idx in groups) {

    min_obs <- ceiling(length(idx) * 2 / 3)

    # Only extract columns for the current condition
    x_group <- assay(se)[, idx, drop = FALSE]

    observed <- rowSums(
      !is.na(x_group) & x_group > 0
    )

    keep_detection <- keep_detection |
      (observed >= min_obs)

    rm(x_group, observed)
  }

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 3. Require valid precursor and protein annotations
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  required_columns <- c(
    "Precursor.Id",
    "Stripped.Sequence",
    "Protein.Group"
  )

  stopifnot(all(required_columns %in% names(rd)))

  keep_ids <-
    valid_text(rd$Precursor.Id) &
    valid_text(rd$Stripped.Sequence) &
    valid_text(rd$Protein.Group)

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 4. Remove decoys, reverse hits and contaminants
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  keep_quality <- rep(TRUE, n_before)

  # Spectronaut: logical Decoy TRUE/FALSE
  if ("Decoy" %in% names(rd)) {

    z <- tolower(trimws(as.character(rd$Decoy)))

    keep_quality <- keep_quality &
      !is.na(z) &
      z %in% c("false", "0", "-")
  }

  # MaxDIA: Reverse flag, typically "+" or blank
  if ("Reverse" %in% names(rd)) {

    keep_quality <- keep_quality &
      not_flagged(rd$Reverse)
  }

  # Spectronaut / MaxDIA: Potential.contaminant
  #
  # Spectronaut uses:
  #   "-" = not flagged
  #   "+" = contaminant
  #
  # MaxDIA may also use "+" / blank.
  if ("Potential.contaminant" %in% names(rd)) {

    keep_quality <- keep_quality &
      not_flagged(rd$Potential.contaminant)
  }

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 5. Proteotypic peptide filtering
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  keep_proteotypic <- rep(TRUE, n_before)
  proteotypic_unknown <- rep(FALSE, n_before)

  if ("Proteotypic" %in% names(rd)) {

    # DIA-NN: explicit proteotypic annotation
    z <- tolower(trimws(as.character(rd$Proteotypic)))

    keep_proteotypic <- !is.na(z) &
      z %in% c("true", "1")

  } else if ("Protein.Ids" %in% names(rd)) {

    # MaxDIA: proxy based on protein identifiers
    # Semicolon-separated multiple IDs are treated as
    # ambiguous protein assignments.
    ids <- trimws(as.character(rd$Protein.Ids))

    keep_proteotypic <- valid_text(ids) &
      !grepl(";", ids, fixed = TRUE)

    proteotypic_unknown <- !valid_text(ids)

  } else {

    # AlphaDIA and Spectronaut:
    # Current Protein.Group annotation alone is
    # insufficient to establish peptide uniqueness.
    #
    # Retain these rows but record unknown status.
    proteotypic_unknown <- rep(TRUE, n_before)
  }

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 6. Combine all filters
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  keep <- keep_detection &
    keep_ids &
    keep_quality &
    keep_proteotypic

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 7. Summarize filtering
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  filter_summary[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Before = n_before,
    Passed_Detection = sum(keep_detection),
    Passed_Quality = sum(keep_quality),
    Passed_Proteotypic = sum(keep_proteotypic),
    Unknown_Proteotypic_After_Filter = sum(
      keep & proteotypic_unknown
    ),
    Retained = sum(keep),
    Removed = sum(!keep),
    Retained_Percent = round(100 * mean(keep), 2)
  )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 8. Filter QFeatures
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  qf_filtered <- qf_one[keep, , ]

  filtered_se <- qf_filtered[["precursors"]]

  # Verify assay dimensions and sample metadata
  stopifnot(
    nrow(filtered_se) == sum(keep),
    ncol(filtered_se) == ncol(se),
    nrow(rowData(filtered_se)) == nrow(filtered_se),
    nrow(colData(filtered_se)) == ncol(filtered_se),
    identical(
      rownames(colData(filtered_se)),
      colnames(filtered_se)
    )
  )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 9. Save filtered QFeatures
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  output_file <- filtered_qf_files[[software]]
  temp_file <- paste0(output_file, ".tmp")

  saveRDS(qf_filtered, temp_file)

  if (!file.rename(temp_file, output_file)) {
    stop("Could not save filtered QFeatures for ", software)
  }

  message(
    software, ": ",
    sum(keep), " / ", n_before,
    " precursors retained (",
    round(100 * mean(keep), 2), "%)"
  )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 10. Release memory before next software
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  rm(
    qf_one, qf_filtered, se, filtered_se,
    rd, cd, keep, keep_detection,
    keep_ids, keep_quality,
    keep_proteotypic, proteotypic_unknown,
    conditions, groups
  )

  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

# ============================================================
# Final filtering summary
# ============================================================

filter_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(filter_summary)

print(tibble::as_tibble(filter_summary), width = Inf)
```
Precursor-level filtering was performed independently for AlphaDIA, DIA-NN, Spectronaut, and MaxDIA. Precursors were retained if they had positive, non-missing intensities in at least two-thirds of the samples within any one experimental condition, preserving condition-specific signals. Annotated decoys, reverse hits, and potential contaminants were excluded. Proteotypic filtering was applied using DIA-NN's explicit annotation and a single-protein-identifier criterion for MaxDIA; however, proteotypic status could not be reliably verified for AlphaDIA and Spectronaut, so these precursors were retained pending further assessment. No minimum peptide count per protein was imposed. Following filtering, AlphaDIA retained 62.5%, DIA-NN 67.8%, Spectronaut 90.8%, and MaxDIA 63.6% of their initial precursors. Spectronaut's higher retention reflects its nearly complete quantitative matrix, whereas detection-frequency filtering had a greater impact on the other pipelines. Differences in software-specific quantification and proteotypic annotations should therefore be considered when interpreting precursor coverage.

```{r visualize_precursor_filtering, fig.width=9, fig.height=5, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
  ) |>
```

## Log-transformation
```{r log_transform_precursors, message=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Log2 transformation of filtered precursor intensities
# Update existing filtered QFeatures files and R objects
# ============================================================

qf_object_names <- c(
  AlphaDIA = "qf_alpha",
  DIANN = "qf_diann",
  Spectronaut = "qf_spectro",
  MaxDIA = "qf_maxdia"
)

for (software in software_names) {

  message("Log2-transforming ", software, "...")

  # Load existing filtered QFeatures
  qf_one <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[[software]])

  # Add log2-transformed assay
  if (!"precursors_log" %in% names(qf_one)) {
    qf_one <- QFeatures::logTransform(
      qf_one,
      base = 2,
      i = "precursors",
      name = "precursors_log"
    )
  }

  # Verify both assays
  stopifnot(
    all(c("precursors", "precursors_log") %in% names(qf_one)),
    identical(
      dim(qf_one[["precursors"]]),
      dim(qf_one[["precursors_log"]])
    )
  )

  # Overwrite existing filtered cache file
  saveRDS(qf_one, filtered_qf_files[[software]])

  # Update the corresponding R object
  assign(qf_object_names[[software]], qf_one, envir = .GlobalEnv)

  message(
    software, ": ",
    nrow(qf_one[["precursors_log"]]),
    " precursors × ",
    ncol(qf_one[["precursors_log"]]),
    " runs"
  )

  rm(qf_one)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

# Verify assay structure in each object
lapply(
  mget(unname(qf_object_names)),
  names
)

# Visualize QFeatures structures
plot(qf_alpha)
plot(qf_diann)
plot(qf_spectro)
plot(qf_maxdia)
```
Following precursor-level filtering, intensity values were log2-transformed using the `logTransform()` function from the QFeatures package to reduce right-skewness and improve comparability of quantitative measurements. The transformed intensities were stored in a new assay named precursors_log, while the original filtered intensities were preserved in precursors. Both assays were retained within each software-specific QFeatures object (`qf_alpha`, `qf_diann`, `qf_spectro`, and `qf_maxdia`), maintaining their metadata and processing relationships for subsequent analysis.

Unlike the other three software packages, Spectronaut has a distinctly multimodal intensity distribution, including a sharp peak near log2 intensity = 0 and a broader low-intensity population between approximately 2 and 7. This is particularly suspicious because almost every Spectronaut precursor has a reported intensity in all 84 runs, despite IsImputed = False throughout.
### Extra filtering step
```{r spectronaut_intensity_floor_correction, message=FALSE}
# Replace Spectronaut raw intensity = 1 with NA
# and reapply condition-aware precursor filtering

se_raw <- qf_spectro[["precursors"]]
se_log <- qf_spectro[["precursors_log"]]

raw <- assay(se_raw)
log_x <- assay(se_log)

# Identify suspected floor values
floor_mask <- !is.na(raw) & raw == 1

n_floor <- sum(floor_mask)

# Replace corresponding values in both assays
raw[floor_mask] <- NA_real_
log_x[floor_mask] <- NA_real_

assay(se_raw) <- raw
assay(se_log) <- log_x

qf_spectro[["precursors"]] <- se_raw
qf_spectro[["precursors_log"]] <- se_log

# Reapply the 2/3 detection criterion within ANY condition
conditions <- as.character(
  colData(qf_spectro[["precursors"]])$condition
)

stopifnot(!anyNA(conditions))

groups <- split(seq_along(conditions), conditions)

keep <- rep(FALSE, nrow(qf_spectro[["precursors"]]))

for (idx in groups) {
  min_obs <- ceiling(length(idx) * 2 / 3)

  observed <- rowSums(
    !is.na(raw[, idx, drop = FALSE]) &
      raw[, idx, drop = FALSE] > 0
  )

  keep <- keep | (observed >= min_obs)
}

n_before <- nrow(qf_spectro[["precursors"]])

# Filter both assays together
qf_spectro <- qf_spectro[keep, , ]

# Verify assay structure and consistency
stopifnot(
  all(c("precursors", "precursors_log") %in% names(qf_spectro)),
  identical(
    dim(qf_spectro[["precursors"]]),
    dim(qf_spectro[["precursors_log"]])
  ),
  identical(
    is.na(assay(qf_spectro[["precursors"]])),
    is.na(assay(qf_spectro[["precursors_log"]]))
  )
)

# Update the existing filtered cache file
saveRDS(qf_spectro, filtered_qf_files[["Spectronaut"]])

# Summarize correction
data.frame(
  Floor_Values_Replaced = n_floor,
  Precursors_Before = n_before,
  Precursors_After = nrow(qf_spectro[["precursors"]]),
  Precursors_Removed = n_before - nrow(qf_spectro[["precursors"]])
)

# Visualize updated QFeatures structure
plot(qf_spectro)

# Release temporary matrices
rm(raw, log_x, floor_mask, se_raw, se_log, keep,
   conditions, groups)
gc(verbose = FALSE)
```

## Normalization
Systematic technical variation between LC-MS runs can introduce differences in measured precursor intensities that are unrelated to biological conditions. Pre-normalization QC revealed batch-associated intensity shifts across the four DIA analysis pipelines. To account for run-level differences, the Median of Ratios method was applied independently to each software's log2-transformed precursor intensities. Normalization factors were calculated using `nfLogMedianOfRatios()` and subtracted from each corresponding run using `sweep()`. The normalized intensities were stored in a new assay named `precursors_norm`, preserving the original precursors and `precursors_log` assays.

```{r normalize_precursors, message=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Median of Ratios normalization for four DIA software tools
# ============================================================

qf_object_names <- c(
  AlphaDIA = "qf_alpha",
  DIANN = "qf_diann",
  Spectronaut = "qf_spectro",
  MaxDIA = "qf_maxdia"
)

normalization_summary <- list()

for (software in names(qf_object_names)) {

  message("Normalizing ", software, "...")

  object_name <- qf_object_names[[software]]
  qf_one <- get(object_name, envir = .GlobalEnv)

  # Calculate log2 normalization factors
 nf_log <- msqrob2::nfLogMedianOfRatios(
  qf_one,
  "precursors_log"
)

  # Check normalization factors
  stopifnot(
    length(nf_log) == ncol(qf_one[["precursors_log"]]),
    all(is.finite(nf_log))
  )

  # Create normalized assay
  qf_one <- sweep(
    qf_one,
    MARGIN = 2,
    STATS = nf_log,
    i = "precursors_log",
    name = "precursors_norm"
  )

  # Verify all three assays
  stopifnot(
    all(
      c("precursors", "precursors_log", "precursors_norm") %in%
        names(qf_one)
    ),
    identical(
      dim(qf_one[["precursors_log"]]),
      dim(qf_one[["precursors_norm"]])
    )
  )

  # Summarize normalization factors
  normalization_summary[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Min_Factor = min(nf_log),
    Median_Factor = median(nf_log),
    Max_Factor = max(nf_log),
    SD_Factor = sd(nf_log)
  )

  # Update existing QFeatures object
  assign(object_name, qf_one, envir = .GlobalEnv)

  # Update existing filtered cache file (no new RDS)
  saveRDS(qf_one, filtered_qf_files[[software]])

  message(software, ": normalization completed")

  rm(qf_one, nf_log)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

normalization_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  normalization_summary
)

print(normalization_summary)

# Check assay structure
names(qf_alpha)
names(qf_diann)
names(qf_spectro)
names(qf_maxdia)

# Visualize processing structure
plot(qf_alpha)
plot(qf_diann)
plot(qf_spectro)
plot(qf_maxdia)
```

```{r evaluate_precursor_normalization, fig.width=14, fig.height=10, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Evaluate Median of Ratios normalization
# Four DIA software packages, 84 runs each
# ============================================================

qf_object_names <- c(
  AlphaDIA = "qf_alpha",
  `DIA-NN` = "qf_diann",
  Spectronaut = "qf_spectro",
  MaxDIA = "qf_maxdia"
)

set.seed(123)

density_list <- list()
median_list <- list()

for (software in names(qf_object_names)) {

  qf_one <- get(qf_object_names[[software]])

  before <- assay(qf_one[["precursors_log"]])
  after  <- assay(qf_one[["precursors_norm"]])

  runs <- colnames(before)

  batch <- dplyr::case_when(
    grepl("^Group1_", runs) ~ "Group 1",
    grepl("^Group2_", runs) ~ "Group 2",
    grepl("^Group3_", runs) ~ "Group 3",
    grepl("^Group4_", runs) ~ "Group 4",
    grepl("^20260331_", runs) ~ "20260331",
    TRUE ~ "Unknown"
  )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. Run-level medians using all finite intensities
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  median_before <- apply(before, 2, function(v) {
    v <- v[is.finite(v)]
    if (length(v)) median(v) else NA_real_
  })

  median_after <- apply(after, 2, function(v) {
    v <- v[is.finite(v)]
    if (length(v)) median(v) else NA_real_
  })

  median_list[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Run = runs,
    Batch = batch,
    Before = as.numeric(median_before),
    After = as.numeric(median_after)
  )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. Sample up to 2,000 values per run for density plots
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  density_list[[software]] <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    lapply(seq_along(runs), function(j) {

      idx <- which(
        is.finite(before[, j]) &
        is.finite(after[, j])
      )

      if (length(idx) > 2000) {
        idx <- sample(idx, 2000)
      }

      data.frame(
        Software = software,
        Run = runs[j],
        Before = before[idx, j],
        After = after[idx, j]
      )
    })
  )

  rm(qf_one, before, after)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

# ============================================================
# Prepare plotting data
# ============================================================

density_qc <- dplyr::bind_rows(density_list) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Before, After),
    names_to = "Stage",
    values_to = "Log2_Intensity"
  )

median_qc_norm <- dplyr::bind_rows(median_list) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Before, After),
    names_to = "Stage",
    values_to = "Median_Log2"
  )

software_order <- c(
  "AlphaDIA", "DIA-NN", "Spectronaut", "MaxDIA"
)

batch_order <- c(
  "Group 1", "Group 2", "Group 3",
  "Group 4", "20260331", "Unknown"
)

density_qc$Software <- factor(
  density_qc$Software,
  levels = software_order
)

median_qc_norm$Software <- factor(
  median_qc_norm$Software,
  levels = software_order
)

density_qc$Stage <- factor(
  density_qc$Stage,
  levels = c("Before", "After")
)

median_qc_norm$Stage <- factor(
  median_qc_norm$Stage,
  levels = c("Before", "After")
)

median_qc_norm$Batch <- factor(
  median_qc_norm$Batch,
  levels = batch_order
)

# ============================================================
# Plot 1: Density distributions before vs. after normalization
# ============================================================

p_density <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  density_qc,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = Log2_Intensity,

  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_density(
    color = "#277DA1",
    linewidth = 0.35,

  ) +

    Software ~ Stage,

  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Precursor intensity distributions before and after normalization",
    subtitle = "84 runs per software; 2,000 sampled intensities per run",
    x = "Log2 precursor intensity",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 12) +

    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),

print(p_density)

# ============================================================
# Plot 2: Median intensity by batch before vs. after

p_median <- ggplot2::ggplot(

    x = Batch,

  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.65,

  ) +

# ============================================================

normalization_qc_summary <- median_qc_norm |>

  dplyr::summarise(
```

### Removing outlier run
One LC-MS run (Group1_c-jun_KO_1) exhibited an atypical precursor intensity distribution across multiple DIA analysis pipelines, most prominently in AlphaDIA and DIA-NN. Given the consistency of this observation across software tools and the availability of additional replicates for the corresponding condition, the run was excluded from downstream quantitative analysis. Normalization was subsequently recalculated using the remaining 83 runs.

```{r exclude_outlier_and_renormalize, message=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Exclude shared QC outlier and repeat normalization
# ============================================================

excluded_run <- "Group1_c-jun_KO_1"

qf_object_names <- c(
  AlphaDIA = "qf_alpha",
  DIANN = "qf_diann",
  Spectronaut = "qf_spectro",
  MaxDIA = "qf_maxdia"
)

# Record the exclusion for reproducibility
qc_exclusions <- data.frame(
  Run = excluded_run,
  Reason = paste(
    "Atypical precursor intensity distribution across",
    "multiple DIA analysis pipelines"
  )
)

# Check that the run exists exactly once in every software
for (software in names(qf_object_names)) {

  qf_one <- get(qf_object_names[[software]])

  runs <- colnames(qf_one[["precursors_log"]])

  stopifnot(sum(runs == excluded_run) == 1L)

  # Ensure all assays contain the same runs
  stopifnot(all(vapply(
    names(qf_one),
    function(a) identical(colnames(qf_one[[a]]), runs),
    logical(1)
  )))
}

exclusion_summary <- list()

for (software in names(qf_object_names)) {

  message("Processing ", software, "...")

  object_name <- qf_object_names[[software]]
  qf_one <- get(object_name)

  n_before <- ncol(qf_one[["precursors_log"]])

  # 1. Remove the outlier column from all linked assays
  keep_runs <- colnames(qf_one[["precursors_log"]]) != excluded_run

  qf_one <- qf_one[, keep_runs, ]

  # 2. Remove previous normalized assay
  #    (its normalization factors included the excluded run)
  qf_one <- qf_one[, , names(qf_one) != "precursors_norm"]

  # 3. Recalculate Median of Ratios normalization factors
  nf_log <- msqrob2::nfLogMedianOfRatios(
    qf_one,
    "precursors_log"
  )

  stopifnot(
    length(nf_log) == 83L,
    all(is.finite(nf_log))
  )

  # 4. Create replacement normalized assay
  qf_one <- sweep(
    qf_one,
    MARGIN = 2,
    STATS = nf_log,
    i = "precursors_log",
    name = "precursors_norm"
  )

  # 5. Verify results
  stopifnot(
    ncol(qf_one[["precursors"]]) == 83L,
    ncol(qf_one[["precursors_log"]]) == 83L,
    ncol(qf_one[["precursors_norm"]]) == 83L,
    !excluded_run %in% colnames(qf_one[["precursors_norm"]]),
    all(c(
      "precursors",
      "precursors_log",
      "precursors_norm"
    ) %in% names(qf_one))
  )

  exclusion_summary[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Runs_Before = n_before,
    Runs_After = ncol(qf_one[["precursors_norm"]]),
    Excluded_Run = excluded_run,
    Min_Factor = min(nf_log),
    Median_Factor = median(nf_log),
    Max_Factor = max(nf_log),
    SD_Factor = sd(nf_log)
  )

  # 6. Update object in R environment
  assign(object_name, qf_one, envir = .GlobalEnv)

  # 7. Overwrite existing filtered RDS file
  saveRDS(qf_one, filtered_qf_files[[software]])

  message(software, ": 83 runs retained and normalization recalculated")

  rm(qf_one, nf_log)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

exclusion_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(exclusion_summary)

print(qc_exclusions)
print(exclusion_summary)

# Final checks
sapply(
  qf_object_names,
  function(object_name) {
    ncol(get(object_name)[["precursors_norm"]])
  }
)
```
The results strengthen the justification for excluding Group1_c-jun_KO_1, particularly for DIA-NN and MaxDIA.

## Aggregation
The objective of aggregation is to summarise the precursor-level intensities into a protein expression value. We illustrate the motivation for summarisation using all peptide-level data for one of the spiked UPS proteins. 
```{r}
protName <- "UPS|P01008ups|ANT3_HUMAN_UPS"
qf[,,"precursors_norm"] |> 
  longForm(colvars = colnames(colData(qf)), rowvars = "Protein.Ids") |> 
  data.frame() |> 
  filter(Protein.Ids == protName) |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = rowname, 
      y = value,
      group = colname) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = condition), size = 3, shape = 21) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjus = 0.5),
        legend.position = "top") + 
  labs(
       subtitle = protName,
       x = "Precursor", 
       y = "log2(norm Intensity)") +
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))
```

1. We can see that data for a protein can consist of many precursors, hence the need for summarisation.
2. We observe that different precursors have different intensities within the same sample (same line). This is because different precursors have different properties and hence differ in their ionisation efficiency, which will influence the detectability in the MS (Challenges).
3. The precursor identification are inconsistent between groups of interest. We can see the low-concentration group (condition a, red) display more missing values than the high-concentration group (condition e, blue). Moreover, which value is missing depends on the precursor characteristics. All the precursors found in the low-concentration group are the most intense precursors in the high concentration group.
4. We also often find outliers, for instance, due to misidentification or fluctuations during MS acquisition.
5. These data also suggest pseudo-replication. The precursor intensities in one same sample (dots connected by a line) are correlated, i.e. they more alike than the precursor intensities between samples (the lines do not perfectly align).

The fact that different precursors have different intensities (2.), may be inconsistently identified (3.) and/or quantified (4.), and show sample correlations (5.) can lead to bias if we use simple summarisation approaches such as summing or averaging the precursor intensities for each sample. Instead, we will resort to more advanced summarisation approaches to accommodate for these issues. Here, we summarise the precursor-level data into protein intensities usin`g maxLFQ`. It is implemented in the `maxLFQ` function of the `iq` package.
```{r}
(qf <- aggregateFeatures(
  qf, i = "precursors_norm", 
  name = "proteins",
  fcol = "Protein.Group", 
#  fun = MsCoreUtils::medianPolish,
#  na.rm = TRUE
  fun = function(X, ...) iq::maxLFQ(X)$estimate
))

qf["UPS|P01008ups|ANT3_HUMAN_UPS", , ]
```
```{r}
qf[, , "proteins"] |>
  longForm(colvars = colnames(colData(qf))) |> 
  data.frame() |> 
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  ggplot() + 
  aes(x = value,
      colour = condition,
      group = colname) +
  geom_density() +
  theme_minimal() +
   labs(subtitle = "Normalised log2 protein intensities")
plot(qf)
```

The data processing is complete.

```{r}
    subtitle = "Number of samples with nonmissing intensity per precursor",
    x = "Number of samples with detected precursor",
    y = "Number of precursor entries"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

# Extract ratio groups from sample names
groups <- sub(
  ".*(ratio0[248]).*",
  "\\1",
  colnames(mat)
)

# Percentage of precursors detected in all 3 replicates
completeness_by_group <- sapply(
  unique(groups),
  function(g) {
    mean(
      rowSums(!is.na(mat[, groups == g, drop = FALSE])) ==
        sum(groups == g)
    ) * 100
  }
)

completeness_by_group
```
- The dataset has a substantial complete-case component. The 22,795 precursors quantified in all nine samples provide a useful subset for exploring quantitative reproducibility without imputation.
- Missingness deserves further investigation. Precursors detected in only some samples may represent low-abundance signals, concentration-dependent detection, or technical variation.
- There is no clear reason to exclude any sample. The current results show relatively consistent coverage, although this is not sufficient to establish quantitative accuracy or replicate reproducibility.

```{r}
# Extract precursor-level annotations
rd <- as.data.frame(rowData(qf[["precursors_norm"]]))

# Extract normalized intensity matrix
mat <- assay(qf[["precursors_norm"]])

# Calculate completeness by species and sample
completeness_species <- lapply(
  unique(as.character(rd$species)),
  function(sp) {

    idx <- !is.na(rd$species) &
      as.character(rd$species) == sp

    data.frame(
      species = sp,
      sample = colnames(mat),
      completeness = colMeans(!is.na(mat[idx, , drop = FALSE])) * 100
    )
  }
) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(
    ratio = sub(".*(ratio0[248]).*", "\\1", sample)
  )

ggplot(
  completeness_species,
  aes(x = ratio, y = completeness, fill = species)
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    alpha = 0.6,
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.12,
    size = 2
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ species) +
  labs(
    title = "Precursor completeness by species",
    subtitle = "Yeast background versus UPS2 spike-in",
    x = "UPS2 spike-in ratio",
    y = "Nonmissing precursor observations (%)"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
Compare precursor completeness by species and UPS ratio.

## Dimensionality reduction plot
A common approach for data exploration is to perform dimension reduction, such as Multi Dimensional Scaling (MDS). We will first extract the set to explore along the sample annotations. We then use the `scater` package to compute and plot the PCA. For technical reasons, it requires `SingleCellExperiment` class object, but these can easily be generated from a `SummarizedExperiment` object.

```{r}
se <- getWithColData(qf, "proteins")
se <- runMDS(as(se, "SingleCellExperiment"), exprs_values = 1)
plotMDS(se, colour_by = "condition", shape_by = "rep") 
```
This plot reveals interesting information. First, we see that the samples are 
nicely separated according to their spike-in condition. Interestingly, 
the conditions are sorted by the concentration.

```{r}
corMat <- qf[["proteins"]] |> 
  assay() |>
  cor(method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs") 

colnames(corMat) <- qf$sampleId
rownames(corMat) <- qf$sampleId
corMat |> 
  ggcorrplot::ggcorrplot() +

```

# Data modeling
Each sample has been synthetically created to contain a constant yeast 
background where human lysates were spiked in at five different concentration. 
Each sample preparation has been replicated three times. So, the key question is
“can our model retrieve the proteins that have been spiked in across the 
conditions?” Moreover, since we know the expected protein abundance in each 
sample, we will also be able to assess how accurate the model can estimate the 
average fold changes between spike-in conditions.

In this experimental design, we can model a single source of variation: 
spike-in concentration. 
All remaining sources of variability, e.g. pipetting errors, MS run to run 
variability, etc will be lumped in the residual variability (error term).

Spike-in condition effects: we model the source of variation induced by the 
experimental treatment of interest as a fixed effect, which we consider 
non-random, i.e. the treatment effect is assumed to be the same in repeated 
experiments, but it is unknown and has to be estimated.

When modelling a typical label-free experiment at the protein level, the model 
boils down to the following linear model: 
$y_i = \mathbf{x}_i^T \boldsymbol{\beta} + \epsilon_i$.

with $y_i$ the$log_2$-normalised and summarised protein intensities in sample 
$i$; $x_i$ a vector with the covariate pattern for the sample encoding the 
intercept, spike-in condition, or other experimental factors; 
$\boldsymbol{\beta}$ the vector of parameters that model the association between
the covariates and the outcome; and $\epsilon_i$ the residuals reflecting 
variation that is not captured by the fixed effects. 
In R, this model is encoded using the following simple formula:
```{r}
model <- ~ condition
```

We estimate the model with `msqrob()`. The function takes the `QFeatures` 
object, extracts the quantitative values from the `"proteins"` set generated 
during summarisation, and fits a simple linear model with `condition` as 
covariate, which are automatically retrieved from `colData(qf)`.

```{r setup, include=TRUE, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE }
qf <- msqrob(
  qf,  i = "proteins",
  formula = model,
  robust = TRUE # improving robustness against outliers
)
```
The fitting results are available in the `msqrobModels` column of the `rowData`.
More specifically, the modelling output is stored in the `rowData` as a
`statModel` object, one model per row (protein).
```{r}
models <- rowData(qf[["proteins"]])[["msqrobModels"]]
models[1:3]
```
## Statistical inference
We can now convert the research question “do the spike-in conditions affect the protein intensities?” into a statistical hypothesis. In other words, we need to translate this question in a null and alternative hypothesis on a single model parameter or a linear combination of model parameters, which is also referred to with a contrast.
```{r}
vd <- ExploreModelMatrix::VisualizeDesign(
    sampleData =  colData(qf),
    designFormula = model,
    textSizeFitted = 4
)
vd$plotlist
```
This plot shows that the average protein $log_2$ intensity for `condition2` 
is modelled by `(Intercept)`, for the `condition4` group by 
`(Intercept) + condtion4` and for the `condition8` group by 
`(Intercept) + condtion8`. Hence, to assess differential abundance of proteins 
between spike-in conditions, we will have to assess all pairwise combinations 
between the spike-in groups, which leads to 3 different contrasts.

This combination of parameters is also called a contrast. Thus, we assess the 
following null hypothesis for this contrast: `condition4 = 0` with our 
statistical test.
`makeContrast()` converts the hypothesis into a formal contrast matrix with 
parameter names as rows and hypotheses in columns. 

```{r}
contrast <- "condition4 = 0"
(L <- makeContrast(
  contrast,
   parameterNames = colnames(vd$designmatrix)
))
```

We can now test our null hypothesis using `hypothesisTest()` which takes the 
`QFeatures` object with the fitted model and the contrast we just built. 
`msqrob2` automatically applies the hypothesis testing to all proteins in 
the data.
```{r}
qf <- hypothesisTest(qf, i = "proteins", contrast = L)
```
The results are stored in the set containing the model, here `proteins`. We 
retrieve the results from the `rowData`. Note, that for this spike-in study we 
know the ground truth, so we also add variable `isUPS` to indicate if the 
protein is spiked (UPS). There is also easier to use the novel getter function 
from msqrob2 `msqrobCollect`.
```{r}
inference <- rowData(qf[["proteins"]])$condition4 
head(inference)

inference <- msqrobCollect(qf[["proteins"]], L)
head(inference)
```

```{r}
alpha <- 0.05 
volcano <- plotVolcano(inference,significanceLevel = alpha) + 
  labs(subtitle = paste0(colnames(L), " = 0"))
volcano 

signif <- inference |>
  filter(adjPval < alpha) |>
  arrange(pval)
knitr::kable(signif)
```
Note, that we return many true positives and one false positive.

We can explore the quantitative data of the significant proteins using a heatmap. 
1. we select the names of the proteins that were declared significant 
between condition A and condition B and extract their quantitative data. 
2. We extract the quantitative data and scale by rows with `assay()`. 
3. We will create a heatmap using the `ComplexHeatmap` package, which enables 
heatmap annotations. We will annotate the heatmap using our model
variables `condition` and `lab`.
4. We now make the heatmap.
```{r}
sig <- inference |> 
  filter(adjPval < alpha) |> 
  arrange(pval) |> 
  pull(feature) #1.

se <- getWithColData(qf, "proteins")
quants <- t(scale(t(assay(se[sig,])))) #2. 

colnames(quants) <- paste0("con", se$condition,"_rep",se$rep) #specific to this dataset to get short colnames
annotations <- columnAnnotation(
  condition = se$condition
) #3.

set.seed(1234) ## annotation colours are randomly generated by default
heatmap <- Heatmap(
                       quants, 
                       name = "log2 intensity",
                       top_annotation = annotations, 
                       column_title = contrast
                       ) #4.
heatmap
```
## All contrasts
With the createPairwiseContrast function we can make all pairwise contrasts for a model.

```{r}
(allHypotheses <- createPairwiseContrasts(
  model, colData(qf), "condition"
  )
)

(L <- makeContrast(
  allHypotheses,
  parameterNames = colnames(vd$designmatrix)
))
```
```{r}
qf <- hypothesisTest(qf, 
                              i = "proteins", 
                              contrast = L,
                              overwrite = TRUE)
```

List with significant deferentially abundant proteins:
```{r}
inferences <- msqrobCollect(qf[["proteins"]], L)

for (j in colnames(L)) #3. 
{
  inference <- inferences |> filter(adjPval < alpha & contrast == j)
  cat("**Contrast:**", j, "= 0 (", nrow(inference |> filter(adjPval < alpha)), "significant proteins)\n\n") #8.
  print(kable(inference |> arrange(pval) |> relocate("feature"), row.names = FALSE)) #9.
  cat("\n\n\n---\n\n") #10.
}

volcanoplots <- inferences |> 
  plotVolcano() +
  facet_wrap(~contrast)
volcanoplots
```
We conduct heatmaps for the significant metabolites for each contrast.

We first extract the normalised assay metabolites_norm along with its colData.
We make an empty list heatmaps to store the plots.
We will loop over the column names of the contrast matrix L
We extract the names of the significant features for contrast i
We extract the quant data for the significant metabolites
We extract annotation
We make the heatmap using the quants data. We do not cluster columns (samples) to keep them together according to the design.
```{r}

heatmaps <- lapply(colnames(L),
                   function(contrast, se, alpha)
                   {
                     sig <- rowData(se)[[contrast]] |> 
                       filter(adjPval < alpha) |> 
                       rownames()
                     quants <- t(scale(t(assay(se[sig,]))))
                     colnames(quants) <- paste0("con", se$condition,"_rep",se$rep)
                     annotations <- columnAnnotation(condition = se$condition)
                     set.seed(1234) ## annotation colours are randomly generated by default
                     return(
                       Heatmap(
                       quants, 
                       name = "log2 intensity",
                       top_annotation = annotations, 
                       column_title = paste0(contrast, " = 0")
                       )
                     )
                   },
                   se = getWithColData(qf, "proteins"),
                   alpha = alpha)

heatmaps
```
## Precursor-level analysis:
525 UPS2 precursor entries rather than all 34,421
```{r, warning=FALSE}
model_prec <- ~ condition

# Extract UPS2 precursor indices
ups_idx <- which(
  rowData(qf[["precursors_norm"]])$species == "ups"
)

# Create a separate QFeatures object
qf_ups <- qf

# Keep only UPS2 precursor entries in the target assay
qf_ups[["precursors_norm"]] <-
  qf_ups[["precursors_norm"]][ups_idx, ]

# Fit robust models
qf_ups <- msqrob(
  qf_ups,
  i = "precursors_norm",
  formula = model_prec,
  robust = TRUE
)

# Inspect results
# 1. Check the model coefficient names
colnames(model.matrix(~ condition, data = as.data.frame(colData(qf_ups))))

# 2. Define the contrast: ratio04 vs ratio02
# 1. Define all three contrasts
L_ups <- makeContrast(
  c(
    "condition4 = 0",               # ratio04 vs ratio02
    "condition8 = 0",               # ratio08 vs ratio02
    "condition8 - condition4 = 0"   # ratio08 vs ratio04
  ),
  parameterNames = colnames(
    model.matrix(~ condition, data = as.data.frame(colData(qf_ups)))
  )
)

# 2. Test all three contrasts
qf_ups <- hypothesisTest(
  qf_ups,
  i = "precursors_norm",
  contrast = L_ups
)

# 3. Collect results for each contrast separately
inference_ups_04_02 <- msqrobCollect(
  qf_ups[["precursors_norm"]], L_ups[, 1, drop = FALSE]
)

inference_ups_08_02 <- msqrobCollect(
  qf_ups[["precursors_norm"]], L_ups[, 2, drop = FALSE]
)

inference_ups_08_04 <- msqrobCollect(
  qf_ups[["precursors_norm"]], L_ups[, 3, drop = FALSE]
)

# 4. Inspect results
head(inference_ups_04_02)
head(inference_ups_08_02)
head(inference_ups_08_04)

# 5. Create volcano plots
alpha_ups <- 0.05

# Create the three plots
p1 <- plotVolcano(inference_ups_04_02, significanceLevel = alpha_ups) +
  labs(title = "ratio04 vs ratio02")

p2 <- plotVolcano(inference_ups_08_02, significanceLevel = alpha_ups) +
  labs(title = "ratio08 vs ratio02")

p3 <- plotVolcano(inference_ups_08_04, significanceLevel = alpha_ups) +
  labs(title = "ratio08 vs ratio04")

# Find common axis limits from the plotted data
plots <- list(p1, p2, p3)

ranges <- lapply(plots, function(p) {
  b <- ggplot_build(p)
  data.frame(
    x = unlist(lapply(b$data, function(d) d$x)),
    y = unlist(lapply(b$data, function(d) d$y))
  )
})

all_xy <- do.call(rbind, ranges)

x_lim <- range(all_xy$x, finite = TRUE)
y_lim <- c(0, max(all_xy$y, na.rm = TRUE))

# Apply identical scales without dropping observations
common_scale <- list(
  coord_cartesian(xlim = x_lim, ylim = y_lim)
)

(p1 + common_scale | p2 + common_scale | p3 + common_scale) +
  plot_layout(ncol = 3)
```
